judgements.justification: A's three-sentence meta-review rests on the chair's own reading ('The reviewers and I ... results are strong') and puts a spotlight above ratings of 6, 6, 6, 7.
Neither committee rested its tier on a forecast of broad impact; both cited the consistency result itself.
The rebuttal moved B's Reviewer_sDSa from 7 to 8, while no Committee A reviewer stated a score change, which widened the score gap.

Two of A's four reviews were thin and misread the setting (Q5eH three sentences at confidence 2; ab3Y questions only, no reply), so A's scores rest on less scrutiny than B's, which include oWmh's detailed 10-hour review.
Only B raised the Theorem 1.1 error, incremental analysis and journal fit, but none of these counted against the paper in B's spotlight.
Both committees heard the same weaknesses (lazy regime, dense theorem, no estimate of R) and both treated them as minor.
sDSa raised the score after the authors' replies, not after reading other reviewers; no other score moved.
No reviewer's rating clearly contradicts their own text; PKyu's praise-only review matches its 8 and A's 6s match mixed texts.
A's reviewers gave 6s at confidence 2 to 3 but did not say they could not judge the paper; B's unsure 9b2J gave a 7, not a borderline score.
B's meta-review copies Reviewer_PKyu's wording ('very well-written, clear') although PKyu, at confidence 2, stood apart from oWmh and 9b2J on presentation, whose complaints the meta-review set aside.
The score gap comes from B's two 8s and the rebuttal raise, not from similar verbal verdicts placed at different points of the scale.
A's chair cited agreement ('The reviewers and I are all in agreement') as the basis for a spotlight although no reviewer rated above 7 or argued for an award.
sDSa raised 'upon reflection' after replies on k-NN rates and citations, not on unverified new results; 9b2J welcomed the promised fix without raising.
B's two-sentence meta-review omits oWmh's and 9b2J's presentation complaints and the disclosed theorem error; A's calls all its reviewers' concerns 'minor comments'.

A's Q5eH said the paper studies infinite-width networks and ab3Y said it bounds random-features models, both wrong, and these readings underpinned their 6s and ab3Y's view that the results are mostly re-proofs.
The authors told B that Theorem 1.1 omitted a sqrt(t*R(U_inf)) term that changed the stated rates; no B reviewer lowered, sDSa raised, and the meta-review does not mention it.
No objection or score change came after the response period closed.
The chairs gave the same tier to different score profiles; there is no split from differing tier cut-offs.
B's chair followed PKyu, not a mean of less-informed reviewers, and B's other high-confidence reviewer, sDSa, also rated 8.
Both committees' concerns were of the same kind and both got the same MNIST estimate and clarifications.
Neither committee had an outlying score; A spans 6 to 7 and B spans 6 to 8 with two at each end.
oWmh and PKyu did not reply to the rebuttal, but neither held an outlying score.
Neither committee had a detractor that the chair set aside.
9b2J preferred a journal because the proofs could not be checked, but still rated 7 and B gave a spotlight, so venue fit held nothing down.
A's meta-review says all reviewers found the results 'strong'; only hyJf wrote that, and three reviewers rated 6.
Most reviewers on both committees replied at least briefly; non-response (ab3Y in A, oWmh and PKyu in B) is similar on both sides.
B counted at full weight PKyu's 8 ('not very familiar with the topic', confidence 2) and 9b2J's 7 (confidence 1, 'I have to trust that the proofs ... will be fine'), lifting B's mean to 7.0.
Neither committee split evenly between accept and reject.

The authors disclosed the Theorem 1.1 error only on B's forum; their same-day reply to A's ab3Y on early stopping did not mention it, so the two committees judged different facts about the main theorem.
The novelty points raised (Nakkiran and Bansal, known data-simplicity results, re-proved calibration links) were checked as correct.
A's spotlight sits above three 'marginally above threshold' ratings, and neither its reviews nor its meta-review give a reason for that tier.
No reviewer objected to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
B had an engaged champion (sDSa), but A's most positive reviewer, hyJf, replied to the rebuttal, and the tiers did not split.
Neither committee judged the promised fixes too large for camera-ready; B accepted the theorem fix on trust.
Neither chair cited input outside the record.
Both committees judged the theory paper by the same standard; both noted the lack of experiments as minor.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score.

reasoning: Both committees recommended a spotlight, so I judged the divergence in how each reached it. A's spotlight comes from its chair's own reading above ratings of 6, 6, 6, 7, justified by a claimed consensus that misstates the reviews and with no stated grounds for the tier (R01, R12, R25, R31); two of A's reviews were thin and misread the setting (R04, R15). B's spotlight follows a mean lifted by low-confidence accept scores (R27) and a rebuttal raise (R03), and its meta-review copies the praise-only reviewer and drops the presentation complaints (R10, R14). The authors disclosed a material Theorem 1.1 error only to B, which did not lower its scores (R16, R29). The stage 1 candidate reasons all map onto existing entries, so I added no reason.
